page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and each core has 1.0 thread. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.67 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a mixed performance profile. In single-core stress-ng CPU tests, the instance performs in the bottom 10%, though Geekbench single-core and text processing scores rank in the top 25%. Multi-core performance across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng falls consistently within the middle 50% average. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the bottom 25%, despite average read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks. Large-model LLM text generation is poor, placing in the bottom 10% for 7B parameter models, while smaller 135M model inference and static web serving throughput remain average.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this server offers a cost-efficient option for workloads that require high core counts but do not demand continuous, dedicated CPU performance. The resource density favors multi-threaded tasks that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, text processing, software compilation, and basic database operations, whereas memory-intensive applications or large-scale machine learning inference may encounter performance limitations.
